slides.title: Stop asking what Muslims differ on
slides.promise: Hold Firmly starts with a different question: what did Allah unite them upon?

slides.head: Applause doesn't give words weight
slides.body: Words take their value from how far they agree with revelation. Not from the speaker's reputation, or how many people applaud.

slides.head: Start with the Qur'an
slides.body: Don't begin with an idea and then search the Qur'an for support. Begin with the Qur'an, and ask what Allah wants from us.

slides.head: Respected, but never above it
slides.body: The work of scholars, thinkers and jurists is human effort that may bring great benefit. It stays subject to the Book of Allah.

slides.quote: The Word of Allah is supreme.
slides.source: The line Hold Firmly's method rests on

slides.head: The Qur'an addresses one Ummah
slides.body: Never a school, a sect or a group. One Ummah, whom Allah Himself named Muslims. So ask first what He united them upon.

slides.head: Disagreement isn't the problem
slides.body: Legitimate scholarly disagreement is not the problem. The problem begins when it turns into fanaticism, partisanship or destructive dispute.

slides.head: Weigh this book too
slides.body: He doesn't ask for agreement. Weigh every idea against the Book of Allah, his own included. If he erred, the Book deserves to be followed.

slides.head: How to weigh differing opinions
items: Start with the Qur'an, not your idea.
Respect scholars. The Book stays above them.
Weigh words by revelation, not applause.
Ask what Allah united Muslims upon.
Weigh every idea, the author's included.
